newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, Council strike deal on interconnections directive.
newsitem.headline: EU, Council strike deal on interconnections directive.

text.p: The European Parliament and the Council of Ministers struck a deal early on Thursday on a key telecommunications liberalisation measure -- the draft directive on interconnections.
A conciliation committee agreed a compromise on the text, COM(95)379, just after midnight after five hours of discussions, a Council official said.
The legislation sets out rules to ensure that phone companies can connect their networks under fair terms once the EU's telecommunications market is fully opened to competition.
The parliament proposed 31 amendments to the Council's common position. EU officials said the conciliation committee agreed the following changes:
-- The common position said that a conciliation procedure for disputes between companies from different member states should be binding only if all parties agree.

The final text says that in principle the procedures for resolving cross-border disputes will be the same as those set out for disputes between organisations in the same country. The result of a dispute-resolution procedure at EU level will be binding.
-- The text says the idea of setting up a European Regulatory Authority to carry out some telecoms regulatory tasks should be assessed when the directive is reviewed by December 31, 1999.

-- "Interconnection" is defined as the physical and logical linking of telecommunications networks to allow the users of one organisation to communicate with users of the same or another organisation, or to access services provided by another organisation.

The parliament had wanted the definition to cover links between telecoms services, but the Council objected because that would have covered service providers without networks such as weather forecasting systems.

-- Integrated Services Digital Networks (ISDN) are not subject to the directive's universal service obligations aimed at ensuring all residents have access to telecoms services at an affordable price. The text says it may be appropriate, however, "in due course" to consider including ISDN.
-- When effective competition is achieved in the EU telecoms market, the need for the directive will be reconsidered -- except for provisions on universal service and dispute settlements.

-- The Commission agreed to accept the parliament's suggestions on "number portability" when it gives its opinion on the assembly's second reading of the directive to apply Open Network Provision to voice telephone.

The common position asked national regulatory authorities to ensure by January 1, 2003 that consumers can keep their phone numbers even if they switch telecoms companies. The parliament wanted them also to ensure that before that happens, consumers could reroute calls to their new number for no fee.
